title: Hammer in a nail that another robot arm is holding
instruction: Hammer the nail 4 cm into the wooden post while the other robot arm holds it, without ever hitting that arm.
context: Two-person jobs like starting a nail need one worker to strike near another's hand. This checks that a policy can use a tool forcefully next to a partner it cannot talk to: light taps while the nail is held, full blows only once the hand is gone.
setup: A 90 x 90 cm wooden table top, 75 cm high. Two YAM arms stand side by side at the back edge, 50 cm apart; the controlled arm is the right one in the screenshot. Distances are from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward, and sideways toward the controlled arm. A wooden post, 10 x 10 cm and 6 cm tall, centred 34 cm forward on the centre line, with a square hole 9.2 mm wide down the middle of its top. A steel nail, 10 cm long, 8 mm diameter with a rounded point and a 22 mm head, 80 g, lies across a small wooden rack (two blocks 3 cm wide and 2 cm high) 26 cm forward and 14 cm toward the other arm, pointing sideways with its head toward the middle. A small hammer, 130 g in all: a 26 cm wooden handle with a flat-sided rubber grip, 20 x 24 mm, and a 2 x 2 x 7 cm steel head. It stands on its face 24 cm forward and 21 cm toward the controlled arm, head toward the middle, the handle level with its end on a wooden rest block. The other arm takes the nail, stands its point in the hole, holds it upright and presses it in; once the nail is 12 mm in and stands by itself, it lets go and draws back. It does the same in every trial.
scoring: The distance the nail goes into the post after the holding arm lets go of it, while the controlled arm holds the hammer, over the distance left to 4 cm, up to 1 (the holding arm presses the nail in about 12 mm itself; that does not count). 0 if the two arms ever touch, or if the hammer ever touches the arm holding the nail; the run stops at the first such contact.
reset_notes: Put the nail back on its rack, the hammer back on its face and rest, and push the nail's resistance in the post back to the top of the hole.
fidelity: Approximate. The wood's grip on the nail is a 20 N friction plug under the point; a nail not yet 1 cm in falls over unless held. Arm links collide as fitted capsules slightly larger than the real ones, so a near miss under about 1 cm can count as a touch. The gripper pinches with up to 50 N through flat pads. The controller uses the manufacturer's joint gains, gravity compensation and motor torque-speed limits. The other arm is scripted on the true scene state.
